A bezel setting is `a jewelry design where a thin strip of metal wraps around the outer edge of a gemstone to hold it safely in place without using prongs`.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/engagement-rings/bezel/)[[2]](https://happyjewelers.com/blogs/education/what-is-a-bezel-setting)

### How It Works

As explained in the [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezel) overview, this ancient method uses a raised metal rim. The jeweler presses or rubs the top edge of the metal over the stone. This creates a smooth, tight border around the gem.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezel)[[2]](https://www.whiteflash.com/jewelry-education/bezel-settings/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x3nJrMTndl4&t=15)[[4]](https://happyjewelers.com/blogs/education/what-is-a-bezel-setting)

### Main Types

- **Full Bezel:** A solid, unbroken ring of metal covers the entire perimeter of the stone. It offers maximum safety.[[1]](https://www.danarebeccadesigns.com/blogs/drd-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-the-bezel-ring-setting)
- **Half Bezel (Partial):** Metal secures only two sides of the stone. This lets more light enter the gem from the open sides.[[1]](https://www.danarebeccadesigns.com/blogs/drd-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-the-bezel-ring-setting)

### Pros and Cons

According to the [Blue Nile](https://www.bluenile.com/blog/fashion/bezel-setting-guide) bezel guide, this style has clear benefits and minor trade-offs:[[1]](https://www.bluenile.com/blog/fashion/bezel-setting-guide)[[2]](https://www.danarebeccadesigns.com/blogs/drd-blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-the-bezel-ring-setting)

- **Pros:** Highly secure, prevents chipped edges, and does not snag on clothing. It has a sleek, modern look.[[1]](https://www.whiteflash.com/jewelry-education/bezel-settings/)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:13364688340822044616,catalogid:14005533321240484243,gpcid:14743234344864377607,mid:576462516930416874&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.bluenile.com/blog/fashion/bezel-setting-guide)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:2134082595244035777,catalogid:9094107591153406022,gpcid:5079191647534140028,mid:576462878442066747&ibp=oshop)[[5]](https://happyjewelers.com/blogs/education/what-is-a-bezel-setting)
- **Cons:** Less light reaches the stone compared to prong settings, which can slightly reduce sparkle unless it is an elevated design. It also uses more metal, making it pricier for fine jewelry.[[1]](https://www.bluenile.com/blog/fashion/bezel-setting-guide)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:13364688340822044616,catalogid:14005533321240484243,gpcid:14743234344864377607,mid:576462516930416874&ibp=oshop)

### Cost

- **Raw Findings:** Simple blank metal bezel cups for crafting cost around $15.[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:9720963835148245186,catalogid:8152801314808344638,gpcid:3785875000810767953,mid:576462828350149300&ibp=oshop)
- **Finished Rings:** Fine gold or platinum diamond rings range from about $1,295 to over $1,900 depending on the metal and diamond choice.[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:2134082595244035777,catalogid:9094107591153406022,gpcid:5079191647534140028,mid:576462878442066747&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:13364688340822044616,catalogid:14005533321240484243,gpcid:14743234344864377607,mid:576462516930416874&ibp=oshop)

If you're planning to buy or make a piece, let me know:

- Are you looking at **rings, necklaces, or earrings**?
- Do you prefer a **full or half** bezel?

I can help you compare options or find the right style.
